# AI Evaluation & Measurement Standard

## 1. Purpose

This Standard establishes Acme Health's requirements for evaluating and measuring the risks and trustworthiness of artificial intelligence (AI) systems throughout their lifecycle. It implements the Measure function requirements that Acme Health has adopted from the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) and related frameworks, and it records, for informational purposes only, the voluntary actions NIST suggests in the AI RMF Playbook.

## 2. Scope

This Standard applies to all AI systems developed, deployed, or operated by or on behalf of Acme Health, and to all personnel involved in the design, development, testing, evaluation, validation, deployment, and monitoring of those systems.

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

AI / ML Engineering owns the AI evaluation and measurement process end to end. AI / ML Engineering is accountable for selecting measurement methods and metrics, executing testing, evaluation, verification, and validation (TEVV) activities, documenting results, tracking identified risks over time, and coordinating the handoff of findings to remediation and governance stakeholders.

Other teams and individuals participate in specific steps as described below, including internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers of the system in question, independent assessors, domain experts, human-factors and socio-technical experts, privacy and security specialists, end users, and affected or potentially impacted communities. AI / ML Engineering remains accountable for the outcome of the process regardless of which participants contribute to an individual step.

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Risk Methods, Metrics, and Effectiveness Review (Measure 1)

#### 4.1.1 Method and Metric Selection (Measure 1.1)

AI / ML Engineering must identify and apply appropriate methods and metrics for measuring AI risks, selecting approaches and metrics for the risks enumerated during the Map function for implementation starting with the most significant AI risks. [NIST AI RMF Measure 1 | NIST AI RMF Measure 1.1]

AI / ML Engineering must document AI risks or trustworthiness characteristics that will not, or cannot, be measured. [NIST AI RMF Measure 1.1]

NIST suggests, among its 12 actions for Measure 1.1, establishing approaches to detect, track, and measure known risks, errors, incidents, or negative impacts; identifying testing procedures and metrics to demonstrate fitness for purpose and AI system trustworthiness; defining acceptable limits for system performance with course-correction suggestions; defining and regularly assessing AI actor competency metrics; identifying transparency metrics and accountability metrics; documenting metric selection criteria including metrics considered but not used; monitoring external inputs such as training data, reused components, and third-party tools; reporting metrics to inform assessments of generalizability and reliability; assessing and documenting pre- and post-deployment performance including existing and emergent risks; and documenting risks or trustworthiness characteristics identified in the Map function that will not be measured, with justification for non-measurement. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 7 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 8 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 9 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 10 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 11 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 12]

#### 4.1.2 Metric and Control Effectiveness (Measure 1.2)

AI / ML Engineering must regularly assess and update the appropriateness of AI metrics and the effectiveness of existing controls, incorporating reports of errors and potential impacts on affected communities; the effectiveness of the employed TEVV metrics and processes must be evaluated and documented, and feedback about the efficacy of measurement approaches must be gathered and assessed. [NIST AI RMF Measure 1.2 | NIST AI RMF Measure 2.13 | NIST AI RMF Measure 4]

NIST suggests, among its 8 actions for Measure 1.2, assessing the external validity of measurements; regularly assessing the effectiveness of existing metrics and controls throughout the AI system lifecycle; documenting reports of errors, incidents, and negative impacts and assessing the sufficiency of existing metrics for repairs and upgrades; developing new metrics when existing ones are insufficient or ineffective; developing and using metrics to monitor, characterize, and track external inputs including third-party tools; determining the frequency and scope for sharing metrics with stakeholders and impacted communities; utilizing stakeholder feedback processes established in the Map function to capture, act upon, and share feedback; and collecting and reporting software quality metrics such as bug rates, severity, and time to repair. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.2 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.2 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.2 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.2 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.2 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.2 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.2 Action 7 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.2 Action 8]

#### 4.1.3 Independent Review (Measure 1.3)

Internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers for the system and/or independent assessors must be involved in regular assessments and updates, with domain experts, users, AI actors external to the developing or deploying team, and affected communities consulted as necessary per organizational risk tolerance. [NIST AI RMF Measure 1.3]

NIST suggests, among its 8 actions for Measure 1.3, evaluating TEVV processes for incentives to identify risks and impacts; using separate testing teams established under the Govern function to enable independent decisions and course correction, tracking and documenting resulting performance changes; planning and evaluating AI system prototypes with end user populations early and continuously, documenting test outcomes and course correction; assessing the independence and stature of TEVV and oversight AI actors; evaluating the interdisciplinary and demographically diverse internal team established under the Map function; evaluating the effectiveness of external stakeholder feedback mechanisms for eliciting, evaluating, and integrating input from diverse groups and for enhancing AI actor visibility and decision making; and identifying and using participatory approaches for assessing impacts arising from changes in system deployment. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 7 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 8]

### 4.2 Trustworthy Characteristics Evaluation (Measure 2)

AI / ML Engineering must evaluate AI systems for trustworthy characteristics. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2]

#### 4.2.1 Test Set and Tool Documentation (Measure 2.1)

AI / ML Engineering must document test sets, metrics, and details about the tools used during TEVV. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.1]

NIST suggests, among its 3 actions for Measure 2.1, leveraging existing industry best practices for documenting all possible aspects of measurement, such as data sheets for data sets and model cards; regularly assessing the effectiveness of the tools used to document measurement approaches, test sets, metrics, processes, and materials; and updating those tools as needed. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.1 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.1 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.1 Action 3]

#### 4.2.2 Human Subjects Protections (Measure 2.2)

Evaluations involving human subjects must meet applicable requirements, including human subject protection, and must be representative of the relevant population. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.2]

NIST suggests, among its 8 actions for Measure 2.2, following human subjects research requirements, including informed consent and compensation, during dataset collection; analyzing differences between the intended and actual population of users or data subjects, including likelihood of errors or negative impacts; using disaggregated evaluation methods across characteristics such as race, age, gender, ethnicity, ability, and region; establishing thresholds and alert procedures for dataset representativeness; constructing datasets in close collaboration with context-of-use experts; following intellectual property and privacy rights related to datasets and represented subjects; evaluating data representativeness through methods such as failure-mode investigation, data quality and sourcing assessment, public benchmarks, bias testing, chaos engineering, and stakeholder feedback; and using informed consent for individuals providing data used in testing and evaluation. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.2 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.2 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.2 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.2 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.2 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.2 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.2 Action 7 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.2 Action 8]

#### 4.2.3 Performance and Assurance Criteria (Measure 2.3)

AI / ML Engineering must measure AI system performance or assurance criteria qualitatively or quantitatively and demonstrate them for conditions similar to the deployment setting(s), with the measures documented. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.3]

NIST suggests, among its 9 actions for Measure 2.3, conducting regular and sustained engagement with potentially impacted communities; maintaining a demographically diverse, multidisciplinary, and collaborative internal team; regularly testing and evaluating systems in non-optimized conditions in collaboration with UI/UX actors; evaluating stakeholder-engagement feedback with human factors and socio-technical experts; collaborating with socio-technical, human factors, and UI/UX experts to translate context-of-use characteristics into test scenarios; measuring systems prior to deployment in conditions similar to expected scenarios; measuring and documenting performance criteria such as validity and efficiency, and assurance criteria such as AI actor competency and experience, relative to ground truth in the deployment context; and documenting differences between the measurement setting and the deployment environment. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.3 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.3 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.3 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.3 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.3 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.3 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.3 Action 7 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.3 Action 8 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.3 Action 9]

#### 4.2.4 Production Monitoring (Measure 2.4)

AI / ML Engineering must monitor the functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components, as identified in the Map function, when the system is in production. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.4]

NIST suggests, among its 7 actions for Measure 2.4, monitoring and documenting how production metrics and performance indicators differ from pre-deployment testing results and considering error propagation and feedback-loop risks when differences are observed; using hypothesis testing or human domain expertise to measure distribution differences between new data and test environments; monitoring for anomalies using approaches such as control limits, confidence intervals, integrity constraints, and machine-learning algorithms; verifying that alerts are in place for distribution differences or detected anomalies; assessing the accuracy and quality of generated outputs against new ground-truth information as it becomes available; using human review, performed by overseers with clearly defined responsibilities and training, to track processing of unexpected data and warn users when outputs may be unreliable; and collecting use cases from the operational environment for testing and monitoring in accordance with organizational policies and regulatory or disciplinary requirements. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.4 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.4 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.4 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.4 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.4 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.4 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.4 Action 7]

#### 4.2.5 Validity and Reliability (Measure 2.5)

AI / ML Engineering must demonstrate that the AI system to be deployed is valid and reliable, and must document limitations of its generalizability beyond the conditions under which it was developed. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.5]

NIST suggests, among its 15 actions for Measure 2.5, defining the operating conditions and socio-technical context under which the system will be validated; defining and documenting the processes used to establish operational conditions and limits; establishing and documenting approaches to measure construct, internal, and external validity using experimental design and statistical methods; assessing and documenting system variance using approaches such as confidence intervals, standard deviation, standard error, bootstrapping, or cross-validation; establishing and documenting robustness and reliability measures; specifying and documenting the assumptions underlying measurement models; using standard software testing approaches such as unit, integration, functional, and chaos testing; using standard statistical methods to test bias, inferential associations, correlation, covariance, variance, and reliability; monitoring operating conditions for performance outside defined limits; identifying TEVV approaches, in consultation with context experts, for exploring system limitations under scenarios that differ from the operational environment; defining post-alert actions such as alerting other AI actors, requesting human review, alerting downstream users, mitigating error propagation, and action logging; logging input data and system configuration whenever the system is used beyond its defined range of validity; and modifying the system over time to extend its range of validity to new operating conditions. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 7 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 8 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 9 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 10 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 11 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 12 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 13 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 14 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.5 Action 15]

#### 4.2.6 Safety (Measure 2.6)

AI / ML Engineering must evaluate the AI system regularly for safety risks as identified in the Map function; the system to be deployed must be demonstrated to be safe, its residual negative risk must not exceed the risk tolerance, and it must be able to fail safely, particularly if made to operate beyond its knowledge limits, with safety metrics reflecting system reliability and robustness, real-time monitoring, and response times for AI system failures. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.6]

NIST suggests, among its 7 actions for Measure 2.6, thoroughly measuring system performance in development and deployment contexts and under stress conditions — including test data assessments, simulations, stress testing under likely scenarios and beyond known limitations, testing against past known incidents or near-misses, and chaos engineering — and documenting the range of conditions under which the system has been demonstrated to fail safely; measuring and monitoring performance in real time to enable rapid response to detected incidents; collecting pertinent safety statistics such as out-of-range performance, incident response times, and down time; aligning measurement with continuous improvement to increase the range of conditions under which the system can fail safely; documenting, practicing, and measuring incident response plans including response and down times; comparing documented safety testing and monitoring information against established risk tolerances on an ongoing basis; and consulting the Manage function for detailed guidance on managing safety risks. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.6 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.6 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.6 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.6 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.6 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.6 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.6 Action 7]

#### 4.2.7 Security and Resilience (Measure 2.7)

AI / ML Engineering must evaluate and document AI system security and resilience as identified in the Map function. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.7]

NIST suggests, among its 10 actions for Measure 2.7, establishing and tracking security tests and metrics such as red-teaming activities, anomalous event frequency, down time, incident response times, and time-to-bypass; using red-team exercises to test the system under adversarial or stress conditions and assess failure modes and recovery, and to evaluate mismatches between claimed and actual performance; documenting red-team results as part of continuous improvement; using countermeasures such as authentication, throttling, differential privacy, and robust machine-learning approaches to increase the range of conditions under which the system can return to normal function; modifying security procedures and countermeasures based on testing and production events; verifying that information about errors and attack patterns is shared with incident databases, other organizations, and system users; developing and maintaining information-sharing practices with AI actors from other organizations; verifying that third-party AI resources and personnel undergo security audits and screenings; and using watermarking technologies as a deterrent to data and model extraction attacks. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.7 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.7 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.7 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.7 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.7 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.7 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.7 Action 7 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.7 Action 8 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.7 Action 9 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.7 Action 10]

#### 4.2.8 Transparency and Accountability (Measure 2.8)

AI / ML Engineering must examine and document risks associated with transparency and accountability as identified in the Map function. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.8]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Measure 2.8, instrumenting the system for measurement and tracking through histories, audit logs, and related information; calibrating user controls in collaboration with UI/UX, HCI, and human-AI teaming experts; testing provided explanations for calibration with different audiences, including operators, end users, decision makers, and decision subjects, to enable recourse for consequential decisions; measuring and documenting human oversight, including the degree of oversight provided, override statistics, reported errors or complaints and response times and types, and adjudication statistics; tracking, documenting, and measuring organizational accountability through policy exceptions, escalations, and documented go/no-go decisions; and tracking and auditing the effectiveness of organizational risk-management mechanisms, including communication lines, roles and responsibilities, and accountability roles such as oversight committees. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.8 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.8 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.8 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.8 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.8 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.8 Action 6]

#### 4.2.9 Explainability and Interpretability (Measure 2.9)

AI / ML Engineering must explain, validate, and document the AI model, and must interpret AI system output within its context, as identified in the Map function, to inform responsible use and governance. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.9]

NIST suggests, among its 11 actions for Measure 2.9, verifying that systems are developed to produce explainable models, post-hoc explanations, and audit logs; using inherently explainable approaches when possible, such as generalized linear models, decision trees, or rule-based models; testing explanation methods and resulting explanations before deployment for accuracy, clarity, and understandability with relevant AI actors, end users, and impacted individuals or groups; documenting model details including model type, data features, training algorithms, proposed uses, decision thresholds, training and evaluation data, and ethical considerations; establishing, documenting, and reporting performance and error metrics across demographic groups and other relevant segments; explaining systems using a variety of methods and testing explanations for fidelity, consistency, robustness, and interpretability; assessing explanation characteristics such as fidelity, ambiguity, interpretability, interactivity, consistency, and resilience to manipulation; testing explanation quality with end users and other groups; securing model development processes against manipulation such as gaming of explanation processes; testing for changes in models over time, including models that adjust based on production data; and using transparency tools such as data statements and model cards to document explanatory and validation information. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 7 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 8 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 9 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 10 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 11]

#### 4.2.10 Privacy (Measure 2.10)

AI / ML Engineering must examine the privacy risk of the AI system, as identified in the Map function, and document the results. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.10]

NIST suggests, among its 8 actions for Measure 2.10, specifying privacy-related values, frameworks, and attributes through direct engagement with end users and potentially impacted groups; documenting the collection, use, management, and disclosure of personally sensitive information in accordance with privacy and data governance policies; quantifying privacy-level data aspects such as k-anonymity, l-diversity, and t-closeness; establishing and documenting access protocols and controls for training or production data containing personally sensitive information; monitoring internal queries to production data for patterns that isolate personal records; monitoring disclosures and inference of sensitive or legally protected attributes and assessing manipulation risk from overly customized content; using privacy-enhancing techniques such as differential privacy when publicly sharing dataset information; and collaborating with privacy experts, end users, operators, and other domain experts to determine optimal differential-privacy metrics for the context of use. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.10 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.10 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.10 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.10 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.10 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.10 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.10 Action 7 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.10 Action 8]

#### 4.2.11 Fairness and Bias (Measure 2.11)

AI / ML Engineering must evaluate fairness and bias, as identified in the Map function, and document the results. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.11]

NIST suggests, among its 24 actions for Measure 2.11, conducting fairness assessments that identify harm types (allocational, representational, quality-of-service, stereotyping, erasure), identify affected groups within, across, and intersecting populations, quantify harms using general and context-specific metrics developed with affected communities, and analyze contextually significant disparities, including for small or intersectional groups; understanding sources of bias in training and TEVV data, including outcome-distribution differences, data completeness and representativeness, proxy features for demographic membership, and systemic bias in unstructured data; leveraging impact assessments and direct engagement with potentially impacted communities to identify and classify impacts, harms, and affected classes; evaluating disability inclusion in bias testing and screening processes; developing objective functions that account for systemic bias and in-group/out-group dynamics; using and customizing context-specific fairness metrics to examine performance variation across and within groups; defining acceptable levels of performance difference and the actions to take when disparities exceed them; identifying groups requiring disaggregated analysis in collaboration with impacted communities; leveraging context experts to investigate substantial measurement differences and root causes; monitoring outputs for bias or performance issues exceeding tolerance and ensuring periodic model updates and recalibration; applying pre-processing, in-processing, and post-processing bias-mitigation techniques and transparent model-selection criteria; collecting and sharing information about outcome differences across groups and considering mediations for differences traceable to past biased decision making; using human-centered design practices and evaluating lifecycle practices for human-cognitive bias sources such as availability, observational, and confirmation bias; working with human factors experts to evaluate presentation bias; and using processes such as diverse staffing and stakeholder engagement to enhance contextual awareness. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 7 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 8 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 9 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 10 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 11 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 12 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 13 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 14 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 15 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 16 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 17 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 18 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 19 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 20 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 21 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 22 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 23 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.11 Action 24]

#### 4.2.12 Environmental Impact (Measure 2.12)

AI / ML Engineering must assess the environmental impact and sustainability of AI model training and management activities, as identified in the Map function, and document the results. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.12]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Measure 2.12, including environmental impact indicators in system design and development plans, including efforts to reduce consumption and improve efficiency; identifying and implementing key indicators of energy, water, and GHG-emission consumption and efficiency; establishing measurable baselines for sustainable operation in accordance with organizational policies, regulatory requirements, and sustainability norms; assessing tradeoffs between system performance and sustainable operation; identifying acceptable resource-consumption and emissions levels and the actions to take when indicators exceed them; and estimating system emissions across the AI lifecycle using carbon calculators or similar processes. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.12 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.12 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.12 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.12 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.12 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.12 Action 6]

#### 4.2.13 Metric and TEVV Process Review (Measure 2.13)

The effectiveness of the employed TEVV metrics and processes must be evaluated and documented as part of the requirement in Section 4.1.2 above. [NIST AI RMF Measure 2.13]

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Measure 2.13, reviewing selected system metrics and associated TEVV processes to determine whether they can sustain system improvements, including error identification and removal; regularly evaluating system metrics for utility and considering descriptive approaches in place of overly complex methods; reviewing selected metrics for acceptability within the end-user and impacted-community population; and assessing the effectiveness of metrics for identifying and measuring risks. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.13 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.13 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.13 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.13 Action 4]

### 4.3 Risk Tracking Over Time (Measure 3)

AI / ML Engineering must maintain mechanisms for tracking identified AI risks over time. [NIST AI RMF Measure 3]

#### 4.3.1 Tracking Approaches, Personnel, and Documentation (Measure 3.1)

AI / ML Engineering must maintain approaches, personnel, and documentation to regularly identify and track existing, unanticipated, and emergent AI risks, based on factors such as intended and actual performance in deployed contexts. [NIST AI RMF Measure 3.1]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Measure 3.1, comparing AI system risks against simpler or traditional models, human baseline performance, and other manual performance benchmarks; comparing end-user and community feedback about deployed systems to internal performance measures; assessing the effectiveness of metrics for identifying and measuring emergent risks; measuring error response times and tracking response quality; eliciting and tracking feedback from AI actors in user-support roles about the metrics, explanations, and system information needed to resolve issues; and eliciting and tracking feedback from AI actors in incident-response and support roles about the adequacy of staffing and resources. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.1 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.1 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.1 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.1 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.1 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.1 Action 6]

#### 4.3.2 Tracking for Hard-to-Measure Risks (Measure 3.2)

AI / ML Engineering must consider risk tracking approaches for settings where AI risks are difficult to assess using currently available measurement techniques or where metrics are not yet available. [NIST AI RMF Measure 3.2]

NIST suggests, among its 3 actions for Measure 3.2, establishing processes for tracking emergent risks that may not be measurable with current approaches, such as recourse mechanisms, bug bounties, human-centered design approaches, user-interaction and experience research, and participatory stakeholder engagement; identifying the AI actors responsible for tracking emergent risks and inventorying tracking methods; and determining and documenting the rate of occurrence and severity level for complex or difficult-to-measure risks when prioritizing new measurement approaches, allocating risk-management resources, evaluating system improvements, and making go/no-go decisions for subsequent iterations. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.2 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.2 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.2 Action 3]

#### 4.3.3 End User and Community Feedback Processes (Measure 3.3)

AI / ML Engineering must establish feedback processes for end users and impacted communities to report problems and appeal system outcomes, and must integrate these processes into AI system evaluation metrics. [NIST AI RMF Measure 3.3]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Measure 3.3, measuring the efficacy of end-user and operator error-reporting processes; categorizing and analyzing the type and rate of end-user appeal requests and results; measuring feedback-activity participation rates and awareness of feedback-activity availability; using feedback to analyze measurement approaches and determine subsequent courses of action; evaluating measurement approaches to determine their efficacy for enhancing organizational understanding of real-world impacts; and analyzing end-user and community feedback in close collaboration with domain experts. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.3 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.3 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.3 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.3 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.3 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.3 Action 6]

### 4.4 Feedback-Informed Measurement (Measure 4)

#### 4.4.1 Deployment Context Consultation (Measure 4.1)

AI / ML Engineering must connect measurement approaches for identifying AI risks to deployment context(s), inform them through consultation with domain experts and other end users, and document the approaches. [NIST AI RMF Measure 4.1]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Measure 4.1, supporting mechanisms for capturing feedback from end users, including domain experts, operators, and practitioners, in settings that allow open sharing of doubts and insights tied to their specific context of use, developed by human-factors and socio-technical experts, and designed to control for interviewer and end-user subjectivity and bias; identifying and documenting approaches, developed in collaboration with human-factors and socio-technical experts, for evaluating and integrating elicited feedback to inform continual improvement; evaluating end-user feedback alongside evaluated feedback from impacted communities; using end-user feedback to investigate how selected metrics and measurement approaches interact with organizational and operational contexts; analyzing and documenting internal measurement processes in comparison to collected end-user feedback; and identifying, implementing, and documenting approaches to measure the effectiveness of and satisfaction with end-user elicitation techniques. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.1 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.1 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.1 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.1 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.1 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.1 Action 6]

#### 4.4.2 Validation of Consistent Performance (Measure 4.2)

AI / ML Engineering must inform measurement results regarding AI system trustworthiness in deployment context(s) and across the AI lifecycle with input from domain experts and relevant AI actors, to validate whether the system is performing consistently as intended, and must document the results. [NIST AI RMF Measure 4.2]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Measure 4.2, integrating feedback from end users, operators, and affected individuals and communities gathered under the Map function as inputs to assessing trustworthiness characteristics, ensuring both positive and negative feedback are assessed; evaluating feedback in connection with the trustworthiness characteristics addressed in Measure 2.5 through 2.11; evaluating feedback on end-user satisfaction with and confidence in system performance, including validity, reliability, explainability, and interpretability; identifying mechanisms to confirm or support system output and end-user perspectives about that output; measuring the frequency of system override decisions, evaluating and documenting results, and feeding insights into continual improvement; and consulting AI actors in impact-assessment, human-factors, and socio-technical roles to assist with analysis and interpretation of results. [NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.2 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.2 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.2 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.2 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.2 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.2 Action 6]

#### 4.4.3 Performance Improvement/Decline Identification (Measure 4.3)

AI / ML Engineering must identify and document measurable performance improvements or declines based on consultations with relevant AI actors, including affected communities, and field data about context-relevant risks and trustworthiness characteristics. [NIST AI RMF Measure 4.3]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Measure 4.3, developing baseline quantitative measures for trustworthy characteristics; delimiting and characterizing baseline operation values and states; using qualitative approaches to augment and complement quantitative baseline measures in close coordination with impact-assessment, human-factors, and socio-technical AI actors; monitoring and assessing measurements as part of continual improvement to identify potential system adjustments; performing and documenting sensitivity analysis to characterize actual and expected variance in performance after system or procedural updates; and documenting decisions related to the sensitivity analysis and the expected influence on system performance and identified risks.
